utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-14/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution. Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Norman Farrell for the Prosecution, with Mr. Wolfgang Sakulin, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For General Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Mitko Naumovski, a lawyer from Zagreb, counsel for Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Naumovski. And for Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: For Mr. Cerkez, Your Honour, Bozidar Kovacic, an attorney from Croatia; and for the first time here in post-judgement phase, co-counsel, Mr. Mikulicic, Goran.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's been some time since we've seen you, Mr. Mikulicic. Welcome back to the case. Now, this is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis. Before we turn to the state of readiness, is there anything that either of the accused, through their counsel, wish to raise as to their state of health or whatever? Right. Well, now, we have now got the briefs filed. However, yesterday I signed an order directed to each of the appellants to file amended grounds of appeal. I thought that I had actually made it reasonably clear, in a decision given, oh dear, on the 11th of September last year, that we expect some form of orderly presentation in these pleadings and that we should not have to look in subsequent pleadings for amendments, additions, variations, or embellishments of matters which should have been in an appellant's brief. That was the decision when, on behalf of Mr. Cerkez, his counsel said, in complaining about the Prosecution getting extra time, that it was an unjustified advantage because it gave the Prosecution an exceptional opportunity to use its brief in the other current matter to answer the arguments which he had filed and added: "Every counsel would do that and every counsel would know how to use the opportunity," a statement which drew a somewhat dusty reply, that: "Whilst it may be that some counsel would take advantage of such an opportunity, the Tribunal does not subscribe to his suggestion that every counsel would do so." It had been made, I thought, fairly clear that we did not want counsel to be adding things where we have to go looking for them in footnotes and in responses, which - I'm sorry, in replies - which should be in an appellant's brief. Now, we want to make it absolutely, abundantly clear that we have to have a document which identifies all of the grounds of appeal taken and where we will find a reference to those grounds of appeal in the briefs. Without that, I am certain that there will be a complaint later on that we have overlooked something, and if we have, it can only be your fault. I want to know precisely how long this is going to take so that we can then make an order when we've seen it and we’ve seen what the grounds of appeal are and we've seen whether there's leave needed to add matters to your appellant's brief. We can then set about giving you a date for the hearing of your appeal. Well, Mr. Naumovski, you're the one who is guilty of putting things in footnotes, and Mr. Kovacic is guilty of putting things in reply. How long will it take you to file a document which sets out your grounds of appeal?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have just read your order of yesterday. I have not thought about the time, but I believe it will take about two weeks. I'm not sure that's exactly how long it will take, but I will start work on it right away, although we are looking through the documents submitted by the Prosecution. However, we'll start on it right away, and I don't think it should take more than two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about you, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would not like to put myself in a situation where I make promises I'm not sure I will be able to keep. It seems to me that my learned friend Mr. Naumovski has been a little optimistic. I would be very grateful if I could be granted three or four weeks, although I am still not certain exactly how much work I have to put into it. But in view of what I can see now, I believe that three or four weeks would be a reasonable time, bearing in mind the strength of our team, the numbers of our team, and the materials being discovered, because we have only just now received the last batch of materials we have to look through. However, I will, of course, abide by Your Honour's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It shouldn't take you four weeks to list your grounds of appeal with references to them. I can understand that you need more time perhaps in order to consider the material which the Prosecution is disclosing to you, but I would like to get something a little earlier than that. I've written down here, just as a date, the 10th of March, which may be somewhere in between the two of you, but that would be nearly three weeks. I think that I'll make that order that that document which was ordered yesterday needs to be filed by the 10th of March. Now, I can see the problem you have in relation to the material, and you will want to, I assume, make an application under Rule 115 in relation to certain of the matters or you perhaps will. So we better start thinking of a cutoff period for that. You sit down, sir. Have you now complied with everything in that order of -- what was it? 15th of November, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's correct. The order with respect to -- yes, we have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And when did you finally give them all the documents? I know you have a schedule, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes. The final disclosure of the last CD with the documents was given when the two counsel arrived yesterday. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What sort of material is involved in it? Your schedule is a helpful one, but I'm not quite sure I can understand how much material there is in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's understandable, Your Honour. The last disclosure, if I can find it, is a CD with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It says just on one CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes, it was on one CD. The total disclosure was somewhere around 40.000 pages, and this was the last of eventually four CDs, as I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Nine hundred and seventy-seven documents. Yes. Well, you, I suppose, have had to look through it at some stage. How long do you think it's going to take for them to finish off looking at this material?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: The material has been reviewed solely for the purposes of disclosure, obviously just to search for the correct categories. We haven't reviewed it specifically. We certainly can. I think our intention, if permitted, was to wait and see what was filed by the appellants as Rule 115 material and from that stage review it and not review material which may not subsequently be filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Well, doing your best on what you've got, how long do you think you're going to need in order to review the material for the purposes of Rule 115? How about you, Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to be quite truthful, there is really a lot of material, and I'm sorry that during our case we were not able to use these materials, because it would have made things much easier for the Court. However, I am doing my best to review these documents. There are about 40.000 pages, as my learned friend has just said, and I have to admit I haven't finished the material that was disclosed earlier. If we are now to have a three-week period to fulfil our obligations, according to your order, then I think that the 10th of March -- well, I'm not sure that we can complete this within a month. I am referring to the CD that is still remaining plus the new one that has just been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I understand that fully. All I'm asking you is how long do you think it will take you to go through the material so that you can then give an estimate on when you'll be able to make your final Rule 115 application? I'm happy to give you longer than the three weeks it takes to put your ground of appeal on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have just said, I will immediately put all my energy into this brief, and if I do so, then I think by the 10th of March I will know where I stand under Rule 115. So I believe that it's the 10th of April of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So you say by the middle of April you'll be able to tell us when you will be ready to file your Rule 115 application. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You see, this is really the next appeal to be heard, and we don't want to leave it any longer than is necessary. That's why I wanted to, at some stage, impose a time limit on your 115 application. Well, if you can tell us by the 10th of April, then certainly we'll be able to impose a time limit and deal with that one as it comes. How about you Mr. Kovacic? Would you be able to tell us by the 10th of April what your intentions are in relation to Rule 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the estimate made by my friend Mr. Naumovski is realistic, and I am certain that by that date we will be able to tell you precisely how much time we would reasonably need to complete our application under Rule 115. Of course, we are already working on it. We already have an outline and general submissions, but for the most part I'm referring to the time we need to expend. We have to put in order the documents so that we can make use of them in a reasonable way. So I believe that by mid-April we will certainly be able to tell you how much time we reasonably need to complete our applications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Well, Mr. Farrell, have you got any suggestion about that? It seems to me fairly reasonable if they've got that much to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I think that's quite reasonable under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And at that stage it may be necessary to have a hearing to determine whether the Rule 115 will be determined prior to the hearing of the appeal or as in my view would be the more appropriate process, to have it heard at the hearing of the appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: The only thing I may caution on is that the Prosecution has been looking through this material for the purpose of any rebuttal evidence. I know that the procedure in Kupreskic attempted to address that issue, and it may be useful that it be addressed again here if necessary, but I want to forewarn Your Honour that depending on what's filed, we can be in a position shortly after they indicate what's to be filed if we feel it appropriate to at least seek leave to respond with our own material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Certainly that's part of the equation, but the Kupreskic appeal, if I may say so, with all due respect to those who took part in it, demonstrated one of the problems with Rule 115 that you can't deal in piecemeal. What may be unimpressive by itself may become impressive when it comes from several different sources. And it also makes it very difficult for the Judges, in effect, to have to get ready twice to consider the same material. As somebody who spent many years in a court of criminal appeal where new evidence or fresh evidence came up regularly, it was always thought better to hear it during the appeal itself, that and any rebuttal evidence. But we shall consider the matter, and my colleagues may have different views, but at least at sometime in April we'll know what the situation is, what's likely to come. You, of course, will have to wait until you see what the application is before you decide upon your rebuttal evidence. But I think we have to keep a bit of a hold on it so the matter just doesn't escape. I'd hate it to lose its place.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: The Prosecution agrees, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Now, is there anything that -- yes, Mr. Naumovski. You wanted to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but if this is the end of today's session, I would like to put forward a technical application. When we read the submissions made on behalf of Mr. Kordic, we noticed a lot of typographical errors, so we would like to ask for permission to submit a corrected copy, where these errors have been corrected, and also to draw up a table indicating the errors that have been corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. If you can have a corrected version, it would be certainly of some assistance, but I hope that you will not think it unfair of me to suggest that we don't want additional material, just corrected material. If you want to add something, you have to make an application to add it, as I have pointed out in the decision yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, of course. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be much easier to read. The small amount of it that I've seen, I wasn't having too much difficulty, but typographical sometimes do produce problems. Now, there's nothing else anybody wants to add? Thank you very much for coming along, and we'll see you sometime after the 10th of April.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
